label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service (Towson) - Aria 3 recalibration, drop-off

Dana, this is the write-up I promised in your thread last month. My Aria 3 has now been through eight days of a civil trial since it came back, so I can say something useful.

The particulars Ellen asks for:

Equipment: Stenvale Aria 3
Work done: full keyboard recalibration, number bar depression sensor replaced, internal cleaning, firmware update, internal battery replaced
Dropped off: Monday 10/19
Returned: Tuesday 10/27, six business days against the ten quoted
Quoted: $285
Paid: $310; the $25 difference is the battery, which I approved
Loaner: yes, an Aria 2, issued at drop-off
Who paid: I did, as I do for all my equipment. No reimbursement from the court.
Warranty: 90 days on the work

Harbor Point is a two-person shop off York Road, with free parking in back. The technician is Gloria Ruark, and her work was good. I had asked for the number bar sensor to be inspected, and she ended up replacing it. My first full day back was expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers, and the number bar did not double a single stroke. It has not done so since. Dana, as that is your complaint exactly, I think it is the most relevant thing I can tell you.

Two other things in her favor. When she found my battery was holding only about 60% of its capacity, she wrote to say what a replacement would cost and that she would not proceed without my approval. That matters to me. The machine also came back with a printed one-page service sheet listing every adjustment, which I have never had from anyone. I think $310 is fair for what was done.

The loaner was less satisfactory. Its tilt arm slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition, and I propped it on a legal pad for the rest of the day. I told Gloria, and she said they would repair it before it goes out again. If you are handed the same unit, check the arm before you leave the shop.

The real weakness is the phone. The line is staffed Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4, and that is all. I called on Wednesday 10/21 to ask about progress. It rang out, and there is no voicemail box set up. Gloria did email me the following day about the battery, having tried to reach me by phone first, so they do communicate; you simply cannot count on reaching them when you want to. For anyone working a Monday docket, that means a machine that fails on Friday afternoon is a problem you carry alone until Tuesday morning. I would not pretend otherwise, and I would like to see them at least set up a voicemail box.

So, should you trust them with your Aria? Yes, I would, and I will go back. The bench work was careful, the price was honest, and it came back four business days ahead of the estimate. Go in knowing how they operate, though. Drop it off in person and use email, not the phone. Choose a week when the loaner will not be carrying anything critical on a Monday or a Friday.

I'm happy to answer questions here.

Maureen
